node.title: Re^2: how portable is the random number generator?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
no guarantees that this won't change in the future

Indeed, just yesterday on P5P: [https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.perl5.porters/2026/01/msg270652.html|Should we upgrade to a new PRNG in core?]

And a relevant note from that thread [https://www.nntp.perl.org/group/perl.perl5.porters/2026/01/msg270655.html|by Russ Allbery]:

The most secure option is to not use any type of pseudo-random number generator and instead rely on /dev/random. If your concern is security, you should not use [doc://rand] and you should not use any other new algorithm that similarly does not use /dev/random. ... If /dev/random is available and you want random numbers for security purposes, you should just use it via [mod://Crypt::URandom], [mod://Crypt::Random], etc.
